# [CS013] WebSocket Origin Check Disabled (websocket-origin-bypass)

A WebSocket upgrader accepts connections from any origin.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-346](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/346.html) |
| **OWASP** | A01:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

WebSocket handshakes carry cookies, and browsers do not apply the same-origin policy to them. A CheckOrigin that returns true lets any website open an authenticated socket as the visitor (cross-site WebSocket hijacking).

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
var upgrader = websocket.Upgrader{
	CheckOrigin: func(r *http.Request) bool { return true },
}
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
var upgrader = websocket.Upgrader{
	CheckOrigin: func(r *http.Request) bool {
		return r.Header.Get("Origin") == "https://app.example.com"
	},
}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [websocket-origin-bypass]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    websocket-origin-bypass: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore websocket-origin-bypass -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** websocket-origin-bypass
```
